claims.statement: The Investment Policy Committee's 2026-03-04 global multi-asset guidance sets the strategic default at 45% global equities, 35% global fixed income, 10% real assets, and 10% private markets for eligible clients; for ineligible clients, the private-markets allocation is reallocated pro rata across liquid sleeves.

The ordinary tolerance bands are ±5 percentage points for equities and fixed income and ±3 for real assets; private markets has no ordinary band because it cannot be traded, and a weight outside a stated band requires approval under the discretion matrix.

The committee adopted reduced duration-diversification underwriting in March 2026, using the rates research's lower-correlation premise to set the equity band at five percentage points rather than the previous seven.

The rates-regime note supplies a working regime assumption and recommends review, but does not itself set global multi-asset bands; the committee plans a 2026 annual review and has not yet changed the strategic weights for that note.

Private-markets exposure is managed through commitment pacing: denominator-effect drift above target is neither a breach nor traded, whereas drift caused by over-commitment is a pacing failure escalated under D.4.

For this allocation guidance, unfunded private-markets commitments are subject to a binding liquidity limit based on the private-markets research framework: they may not exceed two years of liquid portfolio spending.
Any private-markets commitment requires approval and an eligibility determination, and no approval may clear a commitment for a client who is ineligible under the firm's eligibility requirements.

If a research note underlying a band is superseded or withdrawn, the guidance suspends that band and returns to the prior committee-adopted level pending review; managers must escalate rather than re-derive the weight or adopt a replacement note, and the guide is reviewed annually and on cited-note reissue or withdrawal.

The US taxable fixed-income allocation guide is binding allocation guidance for a sleeve comprising US Treasuries, agency MBS, IG corporate credit, and municipal credit; non-US developed sovereign and emerging-market debt are governed in the multi-asset sleeve instead.

For top federal marginal-bracket clients, municipal credit has a 22% target versus an 18% neutral weight, while clients below that bracket use the 18% neutral weight and do not receive the private-activity concentration.

IG corporate credit has a 28% target versus 32% neutral, and its four-point underweight is paired with and funds the municipal overweight; suspending the municipal overweight suspends the corporate underweight and returns both to neutral.

The guide makes municipal implementation limits binding: a 35% maximum in any preferred sector, approval for positions in the named underweight sectors, an 8–15-year municipal duration band, and approval-only extensions beyond 15 years that cannot be granted portfolio-wide.
Municipal tax-loss-harvesting replacements must comply with the municipal sector limit; a replacement that concentrates a preferred sector beyond the limit is a breach when it settles.

Each target has a ±2 percentage-point market-value tolerance measured at month-end, with ordinary out-of-band drift rebalanced in the next monthly cycle; a breach caused by suspension is not automatically rebalanced and instead requires escalation.

When a cited research note is superseded or withdrawn, a manager must suspend the derived weight and escalate to the Committee, documenting the old and replacement notes, derived weights, and affected accounts; the manager may not carry forward the old weight or directly adopt the replacement recommendation.

The guide is reviewed quarterly and out of cycle on re-issue or withdrawal of cited research; the municipal source also calls for immediate review and re-issue on an announced federal tax-treatment change.
The discretion matrix requires documentation of every cleared escalation's condition, authority level, relied-on facts, and date; absent a recorded basis, audit treats the position as unapproved.

Mandate-specific guidance may impose tighter limits but cannot grant discretion broader than the firm-wide discretion matrix; senior portfolio managers may clear one escalation condition per account, while matters beyond senior discretion, accounts with more than one condition, and stated-band exceptions require Committee approval.

Single-issuer positions up to 3% of account market value are within portfolio-manager discretion, senior portfolio managers may take up to 5%, and positions above 5% require Committee approval and a written concentration rationale before becoming subject to the concentrated-position guide.

A concentrated position is more than 15% of a client's liquid portfolio market value, or more than 10% for employer or affiliate securities, and requires documented suitability at acquisition and each annual review covering the holding reason, tax cost of unwinding, and restrictions.

Approval is required regardless of size for stated-band exceptions other than suspension breaches, binding underweight-sector positions, concentrated-position hedges, municipal-duration extensions, and private-markets commitments; the last also requires eligibility to be determined before approval is sought.

A cited research note that is superseded or withdrawn suspends its guide-derived weight; the manager must escalate to the Committee rather than carrying forward, re-deriving, or directly adopting a replacement recommendation, and the record identifies the old note, replacement if any, derived weights, and affected accounts.

A suspension-triggered taxable-fixed-income band breach is not automatically rebalanced; when the municipal overweight is suspended, its paired investment-grade corporate underweight is suspended too and both return to neutral.

Global multi-asset bands use ±5 percentage-point equity and fixed-income bands and a ±3-point real-assets band; private-markets denominator-effect drift is not a breach or trade, whereas over-commitment drift is a pacing failure escalated under D.4.

Trading employer securities on firm discretion during a blackout period is a prohibition that may not be cleared by approval; an ineligible client's private-markets commitment and any regulatory breach likewise cannot be made permissible by investment approval.

Every cleared escalation must record the condition, clearing authority, facts relied on, and date; without a recorded basis audit treats it as an unapproved position and charges it back to the clearing manager's file review.

Private-markets eligibility is a regulatory determination outside portfolio-manager discretion and must be documented before a strategy is offered; eligibility documentation must include the pathway, evidence, decision maker, and date, and eligibility alone does not satisfy suitability or liquidity requirements.

A position is concentrated when it exceeds 15% of the client’s liquid portfolio market value, with a more-than-10% threshold for the client’s employer or an affiliate; the discretion matrix separately requires Committee approval and a written concentration rationale above 5% of account market value and then subjects the position to the concentrated-position guide.

A concentrated position requires a documented suitability determination at acquisition and every annual review, recording the client’s holding rationale, tax cost of unwinding, and restrictions; the file must also show that concentration risk was explained and the client made an informed decision, because preference to hold alone is insufficient.

Hedging a concentrated position requires approval under discretion-matrix §D.3 regardless of size, and tax consequences of collars, prepaid forwards, and exchange funds must be addressed in writing before execution.

For employer securities, the file must record applicable trading windows, blackout periods, pre-clearance requirements, and any Rule 10b5-1 plan; firm-discretion trading during a blackout period is absolutely prohibited and may not be cleared by approval.

Every concentrated position requires a written unwind plan reviewed annually; if the plan is unchanged across three consecutive reviews, that is evidence it is not being applied and must be escalated under §D.4.

Under the discretion matrix, senior portfolio managers may clear one escalation condition per account, while Committee approval is required for matters beyond senior discretion or accounts with more than one escalation condition; every cleared escalation needs a recorded condition, authority, facts, and date, or audit treats it as an unapproved position.

A private-markets strategy may not be offered until client eligibility is determined and documented; eligibility is a regulatory determination outside portfolio-manager discretion, and required commitment approval cannot substitute for it.

For determinations made on or after the order's effective date, the qualified-client determination uses either the Rule 205-3 assets-under-management or net-worth test in SEC Order IA-7104; the order specifies the net-worth treatment of a primary residence and permits jointly held spousal assets for a natural person.

A properly made pre-effective-date qualified-client determination remains valid only with respect to its earlier contract or private-fund investment; it must not be relied upon for a contract or investment entered on or after the effective date.

Accredited-investor status is a separate determination from qualified-client status because Order IA-7104 adjusts only Rule 205-3 dollar tests and leaves Regulation D accredited-investor criteria and the qualified-purchaser definition unchanged.

Eligibility is necessary but insufficient for a private-markets commitment: suitability and the liquidity constraint must also be satisfied, with the research framework underwriting against the client's spending requirement and recommending unfunded commitments not exceed two years of liquid portfolio spending.
The private-markets research allocation applies only after eligibility: the research note states that its allocation view is for eligible clients and does not determine regulatory eligibility.

An adviser relying on an Order IA-7104 determination must retain Rule 204-2(a)(8) records documenting the basis, including the dollar test relied upon and determination date; internally, every determination also records its pathway, evidence, decision maker, and date, and an undocumented basis is treated in audit as no determination.

Frozen research is preserved as the basis of record for positions taken while its edition was effective; a later edition governs new positions only from its own applicability date and does not rewrite the historical decision.

EQ-US-SEMI-CAPEX 2026-02 S.1 supersedes EQ-US-SEMI-CAPEX 2025-06 S.1 for positions taken on or after 2026-03-01, changing the desk view from overweight to neutral while retaining the prior edition as the record for positions taken while it stood.

IRS Revenue Procedure 2025-41 N.3 supersedes FI-US-MUNI-CREDIT 2025-06 M.2's phase-out-threshold premise: the procedure applies from 2026-01-01 with $500,000 unmarried and $1,000,000 joint thresholds, whereas the note says a sufficient threshold cut takes out its after-tax case and recommendation.

IRS Revenue Procedure 2025-41 N.5 preserves the qualified-501(c)(3) treatment relevant to FI-US-MUNI-CREDIT 2025-06 M.5: interest on those bonds is not an AMT item of tax preference, but that preservation does not itself authorize a replacement municipal weight.

DOL Release 2026-31 P.2 and P.3 supersedes FI-US-PENSION-LDI 2026-03 L.2's funding-rule premise by widening the discount-rate corridor and relieving surplus plans from minimum contributions; L.6 identifies altered discount-rate basis or reduced contribution requirements as conditions that end the recommendation.

A manager must suspend, rather than carry forward or mechanically re-derive, a weight derived from superseded or withdrawn research; a suspension-caused band breach is not ordinary drift, and the manager must escalate rather than adopt replacement research directly.

When the taxable fixed-income municipal overweight is suspended, its paired IG-corporate underweight is suspended and both return to neutral; the escalation must identify the note, replacement if any, every derived weight, and affected accounts, while a cleared record must include condition, authority, facts, and date.

The corpus is synthetic: its research, regulator-voiced documents, releases, dates, and figures are invented for the demonstration, while statutory citations are used accurately; it is not real-world investment, legal, tax, or regulatory advice.

Frozen internal research records the edition supporting a position and is revised through a new file, leaving the prior edition as the basis of record for positions taken while it applied; internal guidance is separately living firm material revised in place.
Synthetic documents in external_sources are presented in a regulator voice but state that no reliance is possible, so they are corpus evidence rather than real regulatory advice.

US taxable fixed-income guidance supplies binding portfolio weights and requires a weight derived from a cited research note that is superseded or withdrawn to be suspended and escalated rather than carried forward.
The 2026-02 US semiconductor-capex edition applies to positions taken on or after 2026-03-01 and supersedes the 2025-06 edition.

The global rates-regime research recommends reviewing global multi-asset bands but does not set them; the internal bands guide is the strategic default and requires approval for a weight outside its band.
No private-markets strategy may be offered until eligibility is determined and documented, and eligibility is a regulatory determination outside portfolio-manager discretion.
The IRS AMT threshold procedure applies to taxable years beginning on or after 2026-01-01, and the DOL pension-funding changes apply to plan years beginning on or after 2027-01-01.

A portfolio manager who finds a mandate-cited research note superseded or withdrawn must suspend its derived weight and escalate to Committee with the replacement, derived weights, and affected accounts rather than carry the prior weight or directly adopt the replacement view.
Employer-security trading on firm discretion during a blackout period is prohibited and cannot be cleared by approval.
A suspension-caused US taxable fixed-income band breach is not ordinary drift and must not be automatically rebalanced.
Every cleared escalation must record the condition, clearing authority, specific facts relied on, and date; an escalation without a recorded basis is treated as an unapproved position in audit.

For taxable years beginning on or after 2026-01-01, IRS Revenue Procedure 2025-41 N.3 sets AMT exemption phase-out thresholds at $500,000 for unmarried taxpayers and $1,000,000 for joint filers, superseding the threshold-dependent after-tax basis stated in FI-US-MUNI-CREDIT 2025-06 M.2 rather than changing the continuing AMT preference for specified private activity-bond interest.

IRS Revenue Procedure 2025-41 N.5 preserves qualified 501(c)(3) bond interest as outside the private-activity-bond AMT preference and AMTI, maintaining the distinction relevant to the municipal note’s predominantly qualified-501(c)(3) nonprofit hospital and private-higher-education preferred sectors, but not its predominantly non-qualified airport special-facility sector.

The taxable fixed-income guide ties the top-bracket municipal 22% target and four-point private-activity overweight to M.1/M.2, while the municipal note requires immediate review and re-issue upon a change in the federal tax treatment described in M.2.

When the municipal overweight is suspended because its supporting premise is no longer usable, the guide suspends the paired 28% IG-corporate underweight and returns both allocations to neutral; the suspension is escalated rather than mechanically rebalanced or re-derived by a portfolio manager.

For plan years beginning on or after 2027-01-01, DOL Release 2026-31 widens the permitted corridor around 25-year average segment rates from 10% to 20% in each direction; the release states that this can permit a higher liability discount rate and lower measured liabilities.

Under DOL Release 2026-31, a plan measured above 110% funded under the new corridor is not required to make a minimum contribution for that plan year; a sponsor may elect the excess for qualified replacement-plan transfers or retiree-health accounts, must notify participants within 30 days of electing relief, and receives no new sponsor reversion outside the existing statutory framework.

DOL Release 2026-31 P.2 and P.3 supersede FI-US-PENSION-LDI 2026-03 L.2's funding-rule premise for plan years beginning on or after 2027-01-01: the note says that a rule change allowing surplus release or re-risking can reverse its long-credit demand flow, and L.6 names altered discount-rate basis or reduced contributions as a condition that ends the recommendation.

DOL Release 2026-31 P.5 preserves in full the requirements and restrictions applicable to plans below 80% funded, while leaving benefit accrual and vesting rules unchanged and leaving fiduciary investment standards to their own terms; this limited preservation does not restore the surplus-plan demand premise in FI-US-PENSION-LDI 2026-03 L.2.

SEC Order IA-7104 makes the Rule 205-3 assets-under-management test $1,400,000 and the net-worth test $2,700,000 effective 2026-06-29; the order applies the first immediately after entering the advisory contract and the second immediately prior to entering it.

For net-worth determinations under Order IA-7104, primary-residence value and related indebtedness up to fair market value are excluded, while a natural person may include jointly held spousal assets.

Order IA-7104 preserves a determination for a contract entered into or private-fund investment made before 2026-06-29 only with respect to that contract or investment, and expressly forbids relying on that pre-effective-date determination for a contract or investment made on or after the effective date.

The internal Private Markets Client Eligibility Determination Guide implements Order IA-7104 by requiring its Q.2 pathways for post-effective-date determinations and by preserving and labeling prior-threshold determinations without permitting their use for a new post-effective-date subscription.

Order IA-7104 adjusts only Rule 205-3 dollar tests; it does not adjust Regulation D accredited-investor standards or the Investment Company Act section 2(a)(51) qualified-purchaser definition, each of which continues under its own terms.

Private-markets eligibility is a documented regulatory gate before an offer and is separate from accredited-investor status and from suitability; an eligible client still requires suitability and liquidity work before commitment.
A private-markets commitment requires the eligibility determination before approval is sought, and no approval level may clear a commitment for an ineligible client.

An adviser relying on an Order IA-7104 determination must retain Rule 204-2(a)(8) records showing its basis, dollar test, and determination date; the internal guide additionally requires pathway, evidence, decision maker, and date and treats an undocumented basis as no determination in audit.

EQ-GL-AI-INFRA-POWER edition 2026-01 is a Global Equity Research view published 2026-01-22, applicable to positions taken on or after 2026-02-01, and expressly global rather than limited to one market.

The 2026-01 global AI-infrastructure view overweights regulated utilities with data-centre load growth in their service territories and electrical-equipment manufacturers with transformer and switchgear capacity, while holding no directional view on compute vendors.

The investment premise is that the binding constraint shifts from accelerator supply through 2024 to electrical constraints through 2026—interconnection queue position, transformer lead times, and in some jurisdictions generation adequacy—so economic rent follows the constraint.

The note reports interconnection-study completion beyond 40 months in the largest US market operator and says queue reform reduced speculative-project counts without materially shortening remaining-project timelines; it also models three-to-four-year lead times for highest-voltage large power transformers and no closure of the capacity gap before 2029 from additions announced through 2025.

EQ-GL-AI-INFRA-POWER 2026-01 P.4 modifies EQ-US-SEMI-CAPEX 2026-02 S.4: grid interconnection increasingly gates leading-edge fab siting and caps the rate of new capacity addition rather than the eventual demand level, making power a modifier of the semiconductor-capital-equipment-cycle view rather than a compute-vendor call.

The stated risks are material improvement in compute energy efficiency per unit of useful work, affordability-driven regulatory allocation of interconnection capacity away from data-centre load, and a slowdown in AI capital formation; the latter removes the load-growth premise entirely.
EQ-US-SEMI-CAPEX 2026-02 supersedes the 2025-06 edition for positions taken on or after 2026-03-01, while 2025-06 remains the basis of record for positions taken while it stood.
The 2025-06 edition is an overweight US semiconductor capital-equipment view applicable from 2025-07-01, whereas the 2026-02 edition is a neutral view applicable from 2026-03-01.

The 2026-02 neutral reissue reduces the prior overweight on valuation and late-cycle position rather than deteriorating fundamentals: wafer-fab-equipment spending had risen for six consecutive quarters and deposition-tool lead times had begun to shorten.

EQ-US-SEMI-CAPEX 2026-02 S.3 preserves EQ-US-SEMI-CAPEX 2025-06 S.3: the reissue says the structural customer-concentration argument is preserved in full and not the downgrade reason, while reporting top-three concentration at 46% versus the earlier 51% reading.

EQ-GL-AI-INFRA-POWER 2026-01 P.4 modifies EQ-US-SEMI-CAPEX 2026-02 S.4: grid-interconnection timelines gate leading-edge fab siting in several jurisdictions, capping the rate of capacity addition and changing its shape rather than eventual demand.

The global power view identifies interconnection queues, transformer lead times, and in some jurisdictions generation adequacy as the electrical constraints expected to bind through 2026; it holds no directional view on compute vendors.

The 2025-06 edition identified reductions in either largest logic customer's capex guidance, sustained memory pricing below cash cost, and materially restrictive export controls as conditions that would change its view.

FI-US-IG-SPREADS 2025-09 is an index-level, valuation-driven underweight in US investment-grade corporate credit: it cites unusually tight spreads and limited cyclical-risk compensation, while stable leverage and interest coverage mean it is not a credit-deterioration call.

The IG-spreads note describes an approximate four-percentage-point taxable-sleeve underweight whose proceeds are available for a higher-conviction sleeve position, but the allocation guide—not the research note—sets binding weights and controls suspension of weights derived from superseded or withdrawn research.

FI-US-PENSION-LDI 2026-03 is a long-dated, Single-A-and-better IG-credit overweight based on expected persistent corporate defined-benefit-plan demand through 2028 as surplus plans de-risk by extending duration and rotating into long credit; it is a maturity-bucket flow view that the note says can coexist with the index-level valuation underweight.

FI-US-PENSION-LDI 2026-03 states that a change permitting surplus release, altering the discount-rate basis, or cutting contribution requirements takes out its pension-demand premise and recommendation, and it requires review sooner than 12 months upon an announced funding- or discount-rate-rule change.

DOL Release 2026-31 P.2 and P.3 supersedes FI-US-PENSION-LDI 2026-03 L.2's funding-rule premise for plan years beginning on or after 2027-01-01: the release widens the discount-rate corridor and conditionally relieves plans measured above 110% funded from minimum contributions, with elected excess available for specified uses.
DOL Release 2026-31 P.5 preserves the restrictions for plans below 80% funded, but this does not restore the pension note's surplus-plan demand premise.

FI-US-DURATION-PATH 2026-10 recommends a modest +0.4-year duration position expressed in the 5–10-year sector with a steepening bias, while specifically avoiding long-end duration because of fair-to-cheap term premium, heavy long-end supply, and no expected compression catalyst.

The duration view rests on a central case of one further rate increase over 12 months versus 1.5 priced by markets; the September FOMC statement raised the target range to 3.75%–4.00% but expressly did not commit to a future adjustment sequence.

FED Implementation Note 2026-09-16 I.1–I.4 implements FED Statement 2026-09-16 F.1 by setting the administered reserve-balance and primary-credit rates effective 2026-09-17; it does not modify or extend the statement or provide path guidance beyond it.

FI-US-MUNI-CREDIT edition 2025-06 was published on 2025-06-12, applies to positions taken on or after 2025-07-01, remains marked current and not re-issued, and is the basis of record for taxable-account municipal weightings.

The 2025-06 municipal view is an after-tax overweight, expressed as a two-to-four-percentage-point taxable fixed-income-sleeve increase funded from IG corporate credit and concentrated in high-yield and lower-investment-grade private activity bonds.

For top federal marginal-bracket clients, the allocation guide sets municipal credit at 22% versus 18% neutral and pairs the four-point overweight with a 28% IG-corporate target versus 32% neutral; lower-bracket clients retain 18% municipal and no private-activity concentration.

The M.2 after-tax pickup depends on top-bracket holders avoiding AMT through its then-current phase-out thresholds; it states that a lower threshold bringing a meaningful share into AMT compresses the pickup and takes the M.1 recommendation with it, while fundamentals alone support only neutral to modest overweight.

IRS Revenue Procedure 2025-41 N.3 supersedes the threshold-dependent basis in FI-US-MUNI-CREDIT 2025-06 M.2 for taxable years beginning on or after 2026-01-01 by applying the AMT exemption phase-out above $500,000 for unmarried taxpayers and $1,000,000 for joint filers.

The AMT preference for specified private activity bond interest remains: N.4 says it remains an item of tax preference and is included in AMTI, so the invalidated municipal premise is threshold protection rather than repeal of the preference.

IRS Revenue Procedure 2025-41 N.5 preserves the qualified-501(c)(3) treatment identified in FI-US-MUNI-CREDIT 2025-06 M.5: qualified 501(c)(3) bond interest is not an AMT preference item or included in AMTI, and N.2/N.3 do not apply to it.

The research expresses municipal exposure in the 8-to-15-year band and rejects longer duration and the front end; the allocation guide makes that band binding, caps a preferred sector at 35% of municipal allocation, and requires approval for restricted sectors or extension past 15 years.

M.7-M.8 identify an AMT phase-out threshold cut as the risk that takes out the recommendation and require immediate review and re-issue on a federal-tax-treatment change, but the research remains unreissued; neither residual support nor the preserved 501(c)(3) exception authorizes a manager to calculate a replacement binding weight.

The allocation guide suspends rather than carries forward a derived weight when a cited note is superseded or withdrawn and prohibits automatic rebalancing of a suspension-caused band breach; its text does not resolve the analogous premise-level regulatory supersession without a reissued or withdrawn note, which requires escalation rather than local weight selection.

Private Markets Allocation Framework edition 2025-12, published 2025-12-10 and applicable to positions taken on or after 2026-01-01, is a global research input rather than a client recommendation or eligibility determination.
For eligible clients with a ten-year horizon, edition 2025-12 recommends a 10–20% strategic private-markets allocation, weighted to secondaries and private credit and away from primary buyout.

The note's sub-asset rationale is that secondaries remain the most attractive entry point despite narrowing discounts, private-credit spreads compensate for illiquidity while covenant quality is monitored, and primary buyout should be underweighted rather than avoided because entry multiples are above estimated fair value and exits have not normalised.

The research note recommends underwriting private-markets liquidity against spending needs rather than expected return and limiting unfunded commitments to two years of liquid portfolio spending; the allocation guide constrains that recommendation by making the liquidity constraint binding.

Private-markets implementation is managed through commitment pacing rather than ordinary rebalancing: denominator-effect drift above the strategic weight is not a breach or trade, while over-commitment drift is a pacing failure that must be escalated.

The guide's 10% private-markets weight is a separate strategic default for eligible global balanced clients and is reallocated pro rata to liquid sleeves for ineligible clients, rather than making the research note's 10–20% range binding.

Research does not establish eligibility: the eligibility guide implements SEC Order IA-7104's qualified-client test, requires separate accredited-investor determination, and requires eligibility to be determined and documented before an offer; suitability and the liquidity constraint remain separate pre-commitment requirements.

For entries on or after 2026-06-29, SEC Order IA-7104 sets qualified-client pathways of at least $1,400,000 under management immediately after contract entry or adviser-reasonably-believed net worth above $2,700,000 immediately before entry; pre-effective-date determinations are preserved only for their existing contract or investment, and the order and internal guide require documented determination records.

MA-GL-RATES-REGIME edition 2026-02 is a global Multi-Asset Research framework note, published 2026-02-05 and applicable to positions taken on or after 2026-03-01; it states no directional recommendation.

The edition 2026-02 working assumption is that real short rates have shifted from persistently negative post-2010 levels to a 0%–1.5% through-cycle band; a demand-shock return to the prior regime or fiscal dominance would invalidate that assumption.

Under its higher-real-rate assumption, the note says lower required equity risk premium for duration-like equities and greater fixed-income attractiveness argue for a higher strategic fixed-income weight than bands in force through 2023.

The research desk finds equity-duration correlation unstable and sometimes positive for extended periods, so it does not assume reliably negative stock-bond correlation and recommends materially lower underwriting of duration diversification than the post-2010 sample implies.
The rates note recommends that global multi-asset bands be reviewed against its implications but explicitly does not set bands, which are a committee matter.

Global Multi-Asset Allocation Bands acts on the rates view by underwriting duration's equity-band diversification credit at the reduced R.3 level; the committee adopted this in March 2026, reducing the equity band from seven to five percentage points, while accepting R.1 for review of strategic weights at the 2026 annual review without yet changing those weights.

The committee-set global multi-asset strategic weights are 45% equities, 35% fixed income, 10% real assets, and 10% private markets for eligible clients; ordinary tolerance bands are ±5 percentage points for equities and fixed income and ±3 for real assets, and a weight outside its band requires approval.

A global multi-asset band resting on cited research is suspended if that research is superseded or withdrawn and returns to the prior committee-adopted level pending review; managers must escalate rather than re-derive a setting, carry it forward, or directly adopt replacement research.

Frozen research is not edited after publication: revisions are new editions and the prior edition remains the basis of record for positions taken while it stood, whereas internal guidance is revised in place.
